analysis:
All four units are documentation-only changes: docs/architecture/inference.md (head text lines 2423-2981, plus a new table row at ~1406) and docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (date bump at line 3; new paragraph at ~670-690). No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, or authorization logic changes in the supplied evidence.

Prefix-cache change (relevant to T-041 / SEC-035): the docs describe a new scheduler setting, demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens, which ends a prefill range at the deepest aligned boundary at least 64 tokens below the prompt end. This only moves where complete checkpoints are cut for dense Qwen and is gated on the paged complete store's floor. It does not change the encrypted DBK3 format, HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt scoping, the 30-minute TTL, or the per-donation gate. The doc states that the first/target/latest roles and fleet-novel refusal are unchanged. The new boundary could slightly increase donations or hit rates on growing conversations, which marginally widens the same-account TTFT oracle already accepted under SEC-035. This is not a new class and not a regression visible from docs alone. The actual code (EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift, DemandedShortCheckpointRange.swift) was not supplied. Whether the cut respects the cacheSalt/scope boundary, the storage floors, and the adoption bound is an unverified contract that a code-review pass should check.

inference.md is mostly descriptive text on MiMo media and tool-schema handling, Flint constraints and Qwen4 admission. It states that restoring schemas grants no tool, media, or memory-admission bypass, and that refusal logs are content-free. These are claims in the docs and cannot be checked against the source here.

No findings. Residual question: confirm the code behind the documented demanded-checkpoint change preserves salt scoping and the donation gates; the T-041 threat model may need a note on this.
